forcedChoices.reason: «Realización» in Spanish reads as accomplishment; the section is about the Son becoming real and known to the creature.
«Padre espiritual» also means a spiritual director or godfather; the noun form keeps 'the Father who is spirit'.
English 'must be' can be necessity or inference; «ha de ser» keeps both readings.
'Co-ordinate' here means equal in rank, a status, not a state of being brought into order.

forcedChoices.choice: el Hijo es la Madre Universal
forcedChoices.reason: Spanish forces gender agreement; the title stays feminine as in English, the subject stays masculine.
«compromiso» alone reads as commitment; 'contact-compromise' means a concession in language for contact.
"co-ordinate" here is the adjective of equal rank or status (glossary), so "ser" fits better than "estar", which would suggest a passing state.
"their" refers to the Father and the Son together; "su" keeps the reference without adding words.
